lines.text: Do you know how a homing pigeon finds its way home? Take it hundreds of kilometres away, and it still flies straight back.
One trick is the sun. Pigeons keep an inner clock, so they can use the sun's position like a compass.
When it's cloudy, many scientists think they can sense the Earth's magnetic field. A compass built into the bird.
Closer to home, they follow what they know. Roads, rivers, even smells carried on the wind.
In the First World War, a pigeon called Cher Ami carried a message that helped save nearly two hundred trapped soldiers.
Orbi doesn't need your exact spot. People nearby only ever see your rough area, a patch about forty by twenty kilometres.
